prompts.task: Treat ./service as the project root. The otel-audit report for this fixture is provided at ./service/otel-report.md (the harness strips committed .observe/ inputs, so it is shipped here instead). FIRST create ./service/.observe/ and copy ./service/otel-report.md to ./service/.observe/otel.md. THEN generate detector Terraform for ./service so every output is written under ./service/.observe/ and ./service/.observe/terraform/. Generate the detector Terraform (one signalfx_detector resource per classified metric), variables.tf, terraform.tfvars.example, the .observe/detectors.md report, and the .observe/splunk-configure-verify.md verification file. Do not call any network and do not run terraform.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service/.observe for the resulting files when present, especially ./service/.observe/terraform/detectors.tf, ./service/.observe/terraform/variables.tf, ./service/.observe/detectors.md, and ./service/.observe/splunk-configure-verify.md.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Reads the audit at .observe/otel.md and classifies the checkout metrics into detector categories: latency (http.server.request.duration → P99 threshold) and at least one of throughput or saturation (http.server.request.duration count or http.server.active_requests).

Applies Route-Level De-duplication from detector-classification.md: since the audit states http.server.request.duration already carries an error.type attribute for POST /payment covering the same 502 outcome checkout.payment.errors counts, the error detector reads http.server.request.duration filtered on error.type rather than treating checkout.payment.errors as an independently classified metric. checkout.payment.errors may still appear in detectors.md as a metric merged into that route group, but must not get its own detector resource whose only differentiator from the latency detector is the metric name.

Writes signalfx_detector resources to .observe/terraform/detectors.tf: each resource has a name, program_text with a valid SignalFlow expression referencing the correct metric and a filter('service.name', '${var.service_name}') constraint, and at least one rule block with a severity (Critical/Major/Minor/Warning). Either a detect(when(...)) expression or an against_recent(...) / alerts_and_clears(...) baseline pattern is acceptable. A detector reading http.server.request.duration for the merged error case must add a second filter (e.g. filter('error.type', '*')) so it is distinguishable from the latency detector on the same metric.

Each detector program_text uses the data('<metric>', filter=filter('service.name', ...)).<agg>().publish() pattern with either a detect(when(... > threshold)) tail or an against_recent / baseline alerting tail appropriate for the detector category — a plain publish() without any detection logic is not acceptable, but the skill has latitude to choose threshold vs. baseline-comparison style.

Writes variables.tf with realm, api_token marked sensitive = true, and service_name, plus at least one tunable variable per detector (either a static threshold variable like latency_threshold_s, error_rate_threshold, throughput_min_threshold OR a baseline parameter like fire_lasting_duration, clear_lasting_duration), and a terraform.tfvars.example; never hard-codes a real token or a literal service name in program_text.

Writes .observe/detectors.md summarising the classified detectors, their metrics, severities, and rationale, and hands off to terraform apply or $splunk-detector-publish without performing any network call.

Writes .observe/splunk-configure-verify.md listing each generated detector with at least its resource label (or name), the metric it monitors, and its severity as a verification checklist; full detect condition text is desirable but not required for this criterion to pass.
